independentSolutionSummary: Model the six people as a two-colouring of K6. From any vertex, at least three of the five incident edges share a colour. If any edge among those three endpoints has that colour, it closes a monochromatic triangle; otherwise the three internal edges all have the opposite colour. For five people, a 5-cycle and its complement give a colouring with no monochromatic triangle.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive enumeration of all 2^15 two-colourings of K6; explicit 5-cycle counterexample for K5.

independentSolutionSummary: For one new guest, shift old guest n to room n+1 and use room 1. For one countably infinite bus, send old guest n to room 2n and bus guest k to room 2k-1. The two image sets are disjoint and exhaust the positive integers, so the assignment is collision-free and complete. Countably many buses can be handled by any explicit bijection from N×N to N after reserving a countable subset for existing guests.

Encode two colours by 0 and 1. The back prisoner announces the parity of the 99 visible hats. Each later prisoner subtracts the visible hats and the already-deduced hats behind them from that announced parity, uniquely determining their own bit. Induction gives correctness for prisoners 99 through 1; only the first speaker is not guaranteed.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive verification of the parity strategy for every hat assignment in a six-prisoner analogue.

independentSolutionSummary: A standard checkerboard colouring gives 32 squares of each colour. The specified opposite corners have the same colour, so removing them leaves a 30/32 imbalance. Every edge-adjacent domino covers one square of each colour, hence 31 dominoes would require 31 of each colour, which is impossible.

Pair each positive divisor d of n with n/d. This involution has a fixed point exactly when d^2=n. A nonsquare therefore has only two-element divisor pairs, while a square has exactly one fixed divisor sqrt(n), proving the parity characterization in both directions. The prime-exponent product formula gives the same equivalence.

Assume a complete finite prime list p1,...,pk and set N=p1...pk+1. N is greater than 1, so it has a prime divisor q. Every listed prime leaves remainder 1 on N and therefore cannot be q, contradicting completeness. N itself need not be prime.
computationalChecks: Retained explicit composite Euclid number 2·3·5·7·11·13+1=30031=59·509.

independentSolutionSummary: Inductively 0<=x_n<=2. On that interval, sqrt(2+x)>=x because (2-x)(x+1)>=0, so the sequence is increasing and bounded and therefore converges. Passing to the limit gives L^2-L-2=0, and nonnegativity selects L=2. The stated error identity follows by rationalizing 2-sqrt(2+x).
computationalChecks: Numerical identity and invariant-interval sweep for x in {0,0.1,...,2}; this is a regression check, not the proof.

independentSolutionSummary: The core claim follows because the degree sum is twice the edge count, hence even, so the number of odd summands is even. Equivalently, starting from the empty graph, each added edge flips degree parity at exactly two endpoints.

independentSolutionSummary: Write each selected integer uniquely as 2^k times an odd number. There are exactly n possible odd parts among 1,...,2n, so n+1 selected numbers force two with the same odd part. Ordering their exponents of 2 shows the smaller divides the larger. Sharpness is witnessed by {n+1,...,2n}.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive enumeration of every (n+1)-subset of {1,...,2n} for n<=6 confirms a divisibility pair in all tested cases.

independentSolutionSummary: Let g(x)=f(x)-x. Continuity of f makes g continuous, while f([0,1])⊆[0,1] gives g(0)>=0 and g(1)<=0. Endpoint equality already gives a fixed point; otherwise IVT supplies an interior zero. The same argument works on any interval [a,b].

independentSolutionSummary: Let S_k=a_1+...+a_k. If some S_k is 0 modulo n, that prefix is a valid block. Otherwise n prefix sums occupy only n-1 nonzero residue classes, so two are congruent; their difference is a nonempty consecutive block divisible by n. Equivalently include S_0=0 and apply pigeonhole to n+1 residues.

independentSolutionSummary: For the reflection route, unrestricted paths number C(2n,n). A bad path has a first Up step from y=x to y=x+1; swapping Right/Up on the prefix through that step gives a bijection with paths having n+1 Right and n-1 Up steps, so bad paths number C(2n,n-1) and the desired count is C(2n,n)/(n+1).

independentSolutionSummary: Factor f(x)-f(a)=(x-a)(x²+ax+a²-1). Other equal-height inputs are roots of q_a(x)=x²+ax+a²-1 other than a. Its discriminant 4-3a² gives zero, one-double, or two quotient roots, while q_a(a)=3a²-1 isolates the separate stationary duplication at |a|=1/sqrt(3). For x³-cx the corresponding thresholds are |a|=2sqrt(c/3) and |a|=sqrt(c/3).

independentSolutionSummary: With y_n=1/(1-x_n), direct algebra gives y_{n+1}=y_n+1, hence x_n=1-1/(n+y_0). For x_0<1, y_0>0, so x_n increases to 1. For x_0>1 the orbit becomes undefined exactly when y_0 is a negative integer, equivalently when an iterate reaches x=2; otherwise the translated orbit remains defined and ultimately approaches 1.

independentSolutionSummary: For |a|<2 the radicand is positive on R. Rationalization gives the right limit a/2, while factoring |x| on the left gives R_a(x)=-2x-a/2+o(1). The derivative is negative: it is immediate when 2x+a<=0, and otherwise squaring the positive comparison reduces to a²<4. Thus the range is (a/2,∞). At a=±2 the radical is an absolute value, and for |a|>2 the radicand domain splits into two exterior intervals.

independentSolutionSummary: The original equation has the isolated solution (0,0). Every other solution has x,y nonzero and satisfies 1/x²+1/y²=1, so |x|,|y|>1 with asymptotes x=±1,y=±1. On the nonzero branches, x²+y²>=4 with equality at the four points (±sqrt(2),±sqrt(2)); globally, however, the origin itself is the unique closest point to the origin.

independentSolutionSummary: Squaring gives a_{n+1}²=a_n²+2+1/a_n², hence a_n²>=a_0²+2n and divergence. Summation yields a_n²=a_0²+2n+sum 1/a_k²; the lower bound makes the error sum at most logarithmic, so a_n²/(2n)->1 and positivity gives a_n/sqrt(2n)->1. The same argument with c>0 gives the stated sqrt(2cn) scaling.

The graph equation is (x+1)(y+1)=a+1. For a≠-1 it is symmetric in x,y and direct composition gives T_a(T_a(x))=x; moreover T_a(x) never equals -1, so the second application is defined. Fixed points satisfy (x+1)²=a+1. At a=-1 the original formula instead collapses to the constant -1 on R\{-1}, so it has no valid fixed point and cannot be iterated twice.

independentSolutionSummary: Translate a chosen element to 0. Midpoint closure then gives closure under halving; on the finite translated set, halving is injective and hence bijective, so doubling is also closed. Averaging then doubling gives addition, and finiteness supplies inverses. Thus the translate is an additive subgroup. Modulo a prime the only possibilities are {0} and the full group; for odd composite moduli the solutions are exactly cosets of additive subgroups.

Over F2, final lamps satisfy x_i=y_i+y_{i-1}+y_{i-2}. The zero-effect recurrence y_i=y_{i-1}+y_{i-2} has period three. Cyclic closure gives a trivial kernel when 3∤n and a four-element kernel when 3|n. Hence every target is uniquely reachable in the former case; in the latter, the image has size 2^(n-2), exactly matching the configurations whose three residue-class parities are equal, and every reachable target has four realizing move subsets.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive enumeration of all move subsets for n=3,...,10 confirmed kernel size, image size, residue-class parity obstruction, and realizing-subset multiplicity.

independentSolutionSummary: Equidistance gives ax+by+cz=0; after x=au,y=bv,z=cw this is αu+βv+γw=0 in the cube with α=a²≤β=b²≤γ=c². Direct edge-family tests show four distinct section vertices when γ≥α+β and six when γ<α+β, with equality causing multiple edge incidences to coalesce at cube vertices. For a=b=c the six vertices are the permutations of (1,-1,0), forming a regular hexagon.
computationalChecks: Enumerated all cube-edge intersections for representative γ>α+β, γ=α+β, γ<α+β, and cube cases; distinct vertex counts were 4,4,6,6 respectively.

independentSolutionSummary: A point X=(x,y) is on the diameter circle exactly when r²=ax+by. With b=1-a/2 and a∈[0,2], the right side ranges over the interval between y and 2x, so existence is equivalent to (r²-y)(r²-2x)≤0. This is precisely the closure of the symmetric difference of the two endpoint disks. The λ,L transfer replaces the endpoint values by Ly/λ and Lx.
computationalChecks: Checked a rectangular grid of sample points against the exact solved parameter a and the sign-product criterion; the two membership tests agreed.

independentSolutionSummary: For unit endpoint vectors u,v, OM²=|(u+v)/2|²=(1+u·v)/2. The regular-polygon vertex sum is 0, so conditioned on a fixed endpoint and a distinct second endpoint, the average dot product is -1/(n-1), giving (n-2)/(2(n-1)). Independent draws with replacement have E[U·V]=E[U]·E[V]=0 and therefore mean 1/2.
computationalChecks: Enumerated all unordered vertex pairs for regular n-gons with n=3,...,14; the empirical mean matched (n-2)/(2(n-1)).

independentSolutionSummary: On a line, block starts are position 1 when selected plus each later 0→1 transition, so E[X]=1/2+(n-1)/4=(n+1)/4. On a circle ordinary blocks equal cyclic 0→1 transitions except the all-selected configuration, adding the correction 2^-n; thus E[X]=n/4+2^-n. Replacing 1/2 by p gives p+(n-1)p(1-p) and np(1-p)+p^n.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive enumeration of all subsets for n=2,...,7 matched both the line and circular expectation formulas.

independentSolutionSummary: After n fair halvings the left/right word is a uniformly distributed n-bit integer K, and M_n=(K+1/2)/2^n. This gives mean 1/2 and variance (1-4^-n)/12. With right-half probability p, digitwise expectation gives E[K]=p(2^n-1) and E[M_n]=p+(1/2-p)2^-n. Endpoint conventions matter only for containment questions, not the midpoint distribution.

With arrivals first, q_n=max(0,q_{n-1}+a_n-s), where q_0 is measured just before odd minute 1 and a_n alternates a,b. Let Delta=a+b-2s. If Delta<0, perpetual positivity would force q_{2k}=q_0+kDelta eventually negative, so zero is reached. If Delta>=0, compute q_1 and q_2: a zero there answers yes; if both are positive then q_2=q_0+Delta>=q_0, and monotonicity of the same two-step map prevents any later first zero. Delta>0 gives unbounded even-phase growth; Delta=0 gives a bounded two-phase repeat once positive. The current statement explicitly supplies integer domains, s>0, q_0, starting phase, and event order.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive simulation for 0<=a,b<=6, 1<=s<=5, 0<=q_0<=7 matched the exact emptying criterion through 100 minutes; positive-drift even-phase queues increased by at least Delta each cycle.

independentSolutionSummary: For x>0, f(1/x)=f(x), while (1+x)^2>=4x gives range (0,1/4] with unique maximum at x=1. Cross-multiplication of f(x)=f(y) factors as (x-y)(1-xy)=0, so distinct equal-output inputs are reciprocal. For x/(a+x)^2 the same calculation pairs x with a^2/x, gives maximum 1/(4a), and distinct pairs satisfy xy=a^2.

Any solution of e^x=ax with a>0 has x>0, where a=e^x/x. This function decreases to e at x=1 and then increases to infinity, yielding 0/1/2 solutions for a<e,=e,>e. Replacing x by bx in the exponent moves the minimum to x=1/b with threshold a=be.

Writing e_n=1-x_n gives e_{n+1}=e_n^2 exactly. For 0<x_0<1 this proves monotone convergence to 1 and x_n=1-(1-x_0)^(2^n). More generally every 0<x_0<2 converges to 1, while x_0=0 and x_0=2 lead to 0; the epsilon bound follows by solving |e_0|^(2^n)<epsilon.

The maximal indefinitely iterable real domain is R\{0,1}. It is invariant, f^2(x)=1/(1-x), and f^3(x)=x. Since x^2-x+1=0 has no real root, every real orbit on the safe domain has exact period 3. Translating by c gives the stated g_c domain R\{c,c+1} and the same period.

independentSolutionSummary: Q_a is even with critical points 0 and +/-sqrt(a), heights 0 and -a^2. Equivalently u=x^2 solves u^2-2au-c=0 with u>=0. This yields distinct-real-solution counts 0,2,4,3,2 across c<-a^2, c=-a^2, -a^2<c<0, c=0, c>0. The scaling Q_a(sqrt(a)z)=a^2Q_1(z) is exact.

For fixed x, split at t=x. The two branches are completed squares with unconstrained minimizers 1/2 and -1/2; feasibility produces m(x)=x^2 on |x|<=1/2 and |x|-1/4 outside. Values and first derivatives match at the switches. Replacing t^2 by lambda t^2 moves switches to +/-1/(2lambda) and gives central lambda x^2 and outer |x|-1/(4lambda).

Expanding gives p_a(x)=x^2-sx+1 with s=a+1/a>=2, and every s>=2 occurs. Thus a and 1/a are the only positive-parameter duplication, axes satisfy X=s/2>=1, and vertices lie on Y=1-X^2. For roots a,c/a the same argument gives Y=c-X^2 with X>=sqrt(c).

Nonzero roots are controlled by a^2-4, while turning points are controlled by the derivative discriminant 4(a^2-3). Hence turning points appear at |a|=sqrt(3) and additional real roots only at |a|=2. In the intermediate regime both extrema lie on the same side of the axis because the quadratic factor stays positive. Replacing 1 by c gives thresholds sqrt(3c) and 2sqrt(c).

F is odd because the integrand is even, and F'=(x^2-1)(x^2-9) fixes all monotonicity intervals. F(1)>0 and F(3)<0 force exactly two positive nonzero roots and hence five total by oddness. Integration gives the exact nonzero equation 3u^2-50u+135=0 in u=x^2, producing the stated roots. For the a,b extension, G(b)=2b^3(5a^2-b^2)/15.

The underlying quadratic has roots -2,1 and minimum -9/4, so absolute value reflects the inner arc to height 9/4. Horizontal-line counts are therefore 0,2,4,3,2 for c<0,c=0,0<c<9/4,c=9/4,c>9/4. For roots a<b the transition height is (b-a)^2/4.

For h>0, f(x)-f(x-h)=h(3x^2-3hx+h^2-1). The quadratic discriminant is 3(4-h^2), giving two/one/zero intersections for h<2,=2,>2; at h=2 the translated curves are tangent. The roots tend to +/-1/sqrt(3) as h->0+, and x^3-cx changes the threshold to 2sqrt(c).

Evenness of 1/(1+t^2) makes W odd. Differentiating moving endpoints gives W'=(1-2x^2)/((1+4x^2)(1+x^2)), hence the unique positive maximum at 1/sqrt(2); a direct tail bound gives W->0 at infinity. For k>1, W_k' has numerator (k-1)(1-kx^2), giving maximizer 1/sqrt(k) and the symmetric minimum.

The total label sum is a positive-integer strict monovariant, while the gcd of all labels is invariant under x->x-y. Terminality forces equality across every edge, and connectedness makes the whole labeling constant; gcd invariance identifies that constant with the starting gcd. Disconnected components behave independently.
computationalChecks: On a triangle starting from (1,2,3), legal choices give terminal sequences of lengths 2 and 3, verifying the choice-dependent-duration extension.

independentSolutionSummary: For sizes 1,2,3 the exact possibilities are respectively arbitrary singleton, two distinct residue classes mod 3, and all three residue classes. From size 4 onward, three consecutive residues must be distinct, forcing period-3 residues; each four-term block then has its two interior entries equal to the required trisection points, forcing one common gap not divisible by 3. The converse arithmetic-progression argument is exact.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive search over subsets of {-4,...,4} through size 6 found no mismatch with the stated classification.

independentSolutionSummary: Total counters are invariant and sum of squares drops by 2(a-b)-2>=2 on every legal transfer, proving termination. A terminal unrestricted position has all counts within 1, so total T=qn+r forces exactly n-r copies of q and r copies of q+1. Restricting allowed edges preserves the monovariant but replaces global balance by edge-local balance and can destroy terminal uniqueness.

Prime-by-prime, ab^2 being a cube is e_p(a)+2e_p(b)=0 mod 3, equivalently equality of exponent residues mod 3. This is an equivalence relation and its classes are exactly cubefree kernels. The r-th-power analogue similarly reduces to equality of exponent residues modulo r.

Subtracting adjacent k-window parity equations gives x_i=x_{i+k}. Thus configurations are constant on the gcd(n,k) step-k orbits, giving exactly 2^d choices, and the converse is immediate. Each window contains k/d positions from every orbit class, yielding the stated odd-parity refinement.
computationalChecks: Exhaustive enumeration for every 1<=k<=n<=8 matched the count 2^gcd(n,k) and the orbit characterization.

independentSolutionSummary: Propagating x_{i+1}=s_i/t-x_i/t around the cycle gives x_{n+1}=(-1/t)^n x_1+C. Uniqueness for all readings fails exactly when (-1/t)^n=1: t=-1 for odd n and t=+/-1 for even n. The singular consistency relations are sum s_i=0 for t=-1 and alternating sum 0 for t=1 with even n, after which one parameter remains free.

Composing the two reflections yields translations x->x+/-c. From 0 the reachable set is exactly the subgroup H of multiples of d=gcd(c,m), so all residues are reachable iff d=1. From a general start the orbit is (a+H) union (-a+H), with the two cosets equal exactly when 2a is in H.

|A triangle B| is congruent to |A|+|B| mod 2, so the graph is complete bipartite between even- and odd-cardinality subsets. Pairwise-odd families have size at most 2; pairwise-even families lie in one parity class of size 2^(|U|-1), with equality. The fixed-element symmetric-difference involution proves the parity classes are equal.

A reversal of three consecutive positions only swaps positions i and i+2, so card position parity is invariant. Compressing odd and even positions turns legal moves into arbitrary adjacent swaps in the two lists, proving parity preservation is also sufficient and giving the factorial count. Each move changes exactly one compressed inversion count by 1, so the minimum is I_odd+I_even.
computationalChecks: Breadth-first search for n=3,...,7 matched both the reachable count ceil(n/2)! floor(n/2)! and the inversion-sum distance for every reachable permutation.

independentSolutionSummary: Prime-exponent vectors identify the divisor graph with an integer box grid; each edge changes one coordinate by 1. Therefore distance is L1, shortest paths are the multinomial interleavings of required coordinate moves, and diameter is sum of the exponents. The graph is a tree exactly for N=1 or a prime power; two positive exponent coordinates create a 4-cycle.

The raw drops are unequal, while temperature gaps above 20 are 60,45,33.75 with constant ratio 3/4. Thus T_n=20+60(3/4)^n and the next reading is 45.3125 C. Changing ambient temperature replaces the gap origin; unknown ambient and ratio can be fit from sufficiently many exact nondegenerate readings, while rounded readings support only approximate model comparison.

The adjacent 2x2 condition says each horizontal difference is independent of row, so a_ij=r_i+c_j; the converse is immediate and one additive redundancy leaves m+n-1 degrees of freedom. The argument works modulo q without division. For positive multiplicative diagonal balance, logarithms reduce to the additive case, giving a positive rank-one factorization.

Direct composition gives T^2=5I and expansion of squared lengths gives |T(u,v)|^2=5(u^2+v^2), so distances scale by sqrt(5) and angles are preserved with orientation reversed. Invariant nonvertical slopes satisfy m^2+m-1=0; the vertical line is not invariant. T_a^2=(1+a^2)I and areas scale in magnitude by 1+a^2.

A cell has side L/m; uniform Manhattan distance to its center has mean L/(2m), so mean time is L/(2vm). Adding staffing penalty tau m^2 gives J=A/m+tau m^2 and continuous optimum m^3=L/(4v tau), followed by integer comparison. Euclidean walking changes only the access constant, preserving 1/m and cube-root scaling; nonuniform demand breaks the equal-cell assumption.

On a path, 2x_i=x_{i-1}+x_{i+1} makes first differences constant, so all solutions are arithmetic progressions and endpoints determine the path. On a cycle, a maximum propagates to both neighbors and hence around the cycle, forcing constancy. The same difference/maximum-principle arguments support the stated boundary and fixed-weight transfers.

If a+c=b+d the quadrilateral is a parallelogram and the expression is constant; recentering gives all points exactly when the half-diagonals have equal length, equivalently the parallelogram is a rectangle, and otherwise no points.

independentSolutionSummary: For n distinct elements with sum sigma, the required map is T(x)=(sigma-x)/(n-1). It is injective and hence permutes a finite invariant set. Relative to the mean mu, T contracts distance by 1/(n-1) when n>2, impossible on a nontrivial finite cycle; thus only n=2 works, where T swaps the two values. If the average includes x, the property is exactly mu in S.

For a fair coin, P(N=k)=2^{-(k-1)} for k>=2 and E[N]=3. For 0<p<1, conditioning on the first face gives E[N]=1+p/(1-p)+(1-p)/p, minimized at p=1/2. At p=0 or p=1 the process never changes and N is infinite almost surely.
